title: Define provision-to-ready SLOs + canonical metrics (time-to-ready, step latency, failure rate)
creator: Miles Thornton
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Goal
Define the initial SLOs/SLIs for the Provision-to-Ready automation (Dedicated + shared GPU fleet), plus canonical metric names + tags to unblock dashboards and alerting.

Context
Infra is implementing an orchestration workflow and readiness state machine. SRE needs a clear definition of:
- What “allocated” and “ready” timestamps are
- Which nodes are included/excluded (e.g., quarantine)
- The SLI computation and how to budget errors
- Alert thresholds that are actionable during staged rollout (avoid paging storms)

Deliverables
1) Time-to-ready SLO (P50/P95) + success rate SLO
2) Canonical metric names and tag sets for:
   - end-to-end time-to-ready
   - step latency breakdown
   - failure reasons
   - quarantine counts
3) Initial paging vs ticketing thresholds + rollout-time guardrails

Owners / reviewers
- Owner: Aisha Bello (SRE dashboards & alerting)
- Reviewer: Miles Thornton (reliability/SLOs)
- Consulted: Vanessa Ortiz (Infra/Fleet), Rafael Mendes (SRE), Sean Gallagher (SRE dir)

---
SLO / SLI definitions (v1)

A) End-to-end Time-to-Ready (TTR)
- Start event (AllocatedAt): timestamp when the cloud instance allocation is confirmed and the provisioning orchestrator starts acting on it.
  - Source of truth: provisioning orchestrator event log (NOT Terraform apply start; too noisy/non-deterministic).
- End event (ReadyAt): timestamp when Fleet Readiness Service records state transition into Ready.
  - Source of truth: control-plane write by Fleet Readiness Service.
- TTR = ReadyAt - AllocatedAt
- Scope: Dedicated pools + staged shared fleet pools that use the new provisioning workflow.
- Inclusion criteria:
  - Nodes that reached Ready in the measurement window.
- Exclusion criteria (from “latency” SLI, but counted in availability/failure SLI):
  - Nodes that never reach Ready and end in Quarantined (or terminated) within the window.

B) Provisioning Success Rate
- Definition: % of allocated nodes that reach Ready within a target time bound (see objectives below).
- Failure includes:
  - Quarantined due to repeated validation failure
  - Terminated/reimaged due to provisioning automation failure
  - Stuck in Provisioning/Validating beyond max time bound

C) Error budget accounting
- Latency SLO is tracked on successful nodes (TTR distribution).
- Reliability SLO tracks success/failure outcomes on all allocations.
- During staged rollout, error budget burn alerts are ticket-only until baseline stabilizes (see Alerting policy).

---
Objectives (initial proposal based on baseline sheet + Infra expectations)

1) Time-to-Ready (latency) SLO
- P50 TTR <= 18 minutes (weekly window)
- P95 TTR <= 35 minutes (weekly window)
Notes:
- Baseline (pre-sprint) P95 in us-east/A100 was commonly 55–75 minutes depending on manual steps and join/validation flakiness.
- These targets are intentionally conservative for v1 to avoid constant SLO violation while rollout is partial.

2) Success rate SLO
- >= 98.5% of allocations reach Ready within 60 minutes (weekly window)
- “Within 60 minutes” aligns with ops expectations for Dedicated expansions and keeps quarantine from silently reducing effective capacity.

3) Step-level guardrail (non-SLO, but alertable)
- Any single step exceeding 2x its trailing 7d median for > 30m is investigated (ticket initially).

---
Canonical metrics (names + types + required tags)

Metric naming principles
- Use stable, low-cardinality tags (NO node_id / instance_id).
- Prefer enumerated values for step and failure_reason.
- Keep pool identifiers out of tags unless they’re coarse (pool_type, tier). Pool IDs are logged (not tagged).

1) End-to-end TTR
- fleet.provision_to_ready.ttr_seconds (HISTOGRAM)
  - Unit: seconds
  - Tags:
    - region (e.g., us-east-1)
    - gpu_type (e.g., a100, h100, l40s)
    - pool_type (dedicated|shared)
    - image_channel (candidate|stable)
    - orchestrator_version (semantic or git sha short; optional but recommended)
    - result (success|failure)

2) Step latency
- fleet.provision_to_ready.step_seconds (HISTOGRAM)
  - Tags:
    - region
    - gpu_type
    - pool_type
    - image_channel
    - step (enum): allocate_confirmed, image_boot, kubelet_join, runtime_install_check, gpu_health, driver_parity, network_smoke, storage_smoke, nccl_smoke, inference_canary, finalize_ready
    - result (success|failure|timeout|skipped)

3) State transitions (for SLI computation + stuck detection)
- fleet.readiness.state_transition_total (COUNTER)
  - Tags:
    - from_state (allocated|provisioning|validating|ready|quarantined)
    - to_state (allocated|provisioning|validating|ready|quarantined)
    - region
    - gpu_type
    - pool_type

4) Failures / quarantine
- fleet.provision_to_ready.failure_total (COUNTER)
  - Tags:
    - step
    - failure_reason (enum; see below)
    - region
    - gpu_type
    - pool_type
    - image_channel

- fleet.readiness.quarantine_total (COUNTER)
  - Tags:
    - reason (enum)
    - region
    - gpu_type
    - pool_type

Failure reason enum (initial)
- driver_mismatch
- driver_install_failed
- kubelet_join_failed
- cni_not_ready
- disk_mount_failed
- gpu_ecc_exceeded
- nvidia_xid_error
- nccl_timeout
- nccl_perf_regression
- inference_canary_failed
- validation_agent_unhealthy
- unknown

---
Alerting policy (initial; staged rollout safe)

Paging alerts (P0/P1 page)
1) Readiness success rate drop (hard failure)
- Condition: success rate < 95% over 30 minutes for a single region+gpu_type cohort AND allocations >= 10
- Action: page Infra on-call + notify SRE channel
- Rationale: indicates systemic break (image, join, fabric) likely impacting capacity.

2) Quarantine spike (capacity risk)
- Condition: quarantine_total rate >= 5 / 30m for a region+gpu_type cohort OR quarantined_nodes > 10% of newly allocated nodes in 1h
- Action: page Infra on-call; open incident if customer Dedicated pool impacted.

Ticket (non-paging) alerts
1) Latency regression (TTR)
- Condition: P95 TTR > 45 minutes for 2 consecutive hours for a cohort AND allocations >= 20
- Action: create ticket + tag #eng-sre for review; no paging during first 2 weeks of rollout.

2) Step latency regression
- Condition: step_seconds P95 exceeds 2x trailing 7d baseline for 1h
- Action: ticket, routed to component owner.

Rollout-time guardrails
- No new paging alerts enabled until:
  - metric cardinality is validated (no per-node tags)
  - dashboards are live and reviewed by Infra + SRE
  - at least 72h of staged rollout data exists

---
Success criteria / acceptance
- SLOs and definitions published to Confluence (eng-sre) and linked from provisioning overview doc.
- Metric names + tags agreed and referenced by:
  - dashboard PR
  - SLI computation PR
- Alert thresholds reviewed by Sean + Vanessa and explicitly marked as “v1; expected to tune.”

---
Open questions (tracked as follow-ups)
- Whether to include “ready but removed from serving pool due to post-canary regression” as failure vs separate category.
- How to model manual operator overrides (e.g., forced Ready) in SLI; proposed: count as success but tag result=forced for audit.

Resolution

- Implementation is unblocked for ENG-4827 (dashboards) and SLI computation in slo-toolkit/pr-309.

Follow-ups
